report.summary: I reviewed the final ordinary-covered canonical branch in lib/delivery-assessment.ts (lines 363-374) against the V3 source-witness path (lines 344-353), the witness producer (positive-literal-source-witness.ts) and its verifier (source-business-evidence.ts), and against tests/positive-literal-assessment.test.ts. The new branch is gated by encoding "catalog_slots", raw item.status supported, business.kind unchanged (witness.kind covered only comes from unchanged evidence), and literal.kind covered (which requires an exact same-file p/li owner, exactly one body occurrence, an exact model citation of the complete owner, and the valid snapshot budget). When those conditions hold it replaces only the explanation. Status, citations, evidenceNeed and obligations are unchanged, and every later guard (presence, exact-copy, label, universal tag/list, no-citation) still runs. The new test at line 55 uses a dynamic=false fixture with a real catalog entry and asserts supported status, no evidenceNeed, canonical prose, the owner-only citation, and no withheld-risk adjustments. The earlier dynamic-unknown test at line 44, the mismatch, fail-priority, mixed/short-citation, V2/legacy and operation-tail cases are untouched and consistent with the new branch. I found no concrete correctness, security or product-flow defect within the requested narrow scope.
limitations: Source review only. I did not run tests, typecheck, the application or any runtime probe, so I make no runtime, visible, update or pass/fail claim.

Scope was limited to the packet files and to the final ordinary-covered canonical branch (delivery-assessment.ts lines 363-374) plus its immediate guards. Module design, normalization, duplicate/allowed-occurrence policy, the dynamic-unknown bypass and other guards were not reopened.

Files referenced but not supplied were not inspected: contracts.ts, assessment-citation-catalog.ts, source-presence-evidence.ts, exact-copy-evidence.ts, assessment-publication-policy.ts, business-checks.ts, assessment-evidence-scope.ts and the risk/limitation publication path.
The packet's substrings omit code-comment-only text in places (for example inside source-business-evidence.ts near line 71); any conclusion about those omitted comments is unsupported.
I did not verify the reported 'all 18 tests pass' or the claimed post-cycle-26 tests, because no execution was permitted.
No application API, browser, payment or award/judge outcome is established, and no overall award or superiority claim is made.
